title: LHD Cycle Evaluation
body: Every minute lost in load, haul, dump, or return is a minute the fleet isn't moving material — and at ADW right now, with utilization gaps of 6-6.5 idle hours per shift against a 2.5-3 hour best-case, those minutes are the difference between hitting daily target and another shortfall meeting. You can't fix a bottleneck you haven't located.
keyPoints: The cycle breaks into five stages — load, haul (loaded), dump, return (empty), idle. Time each one separately, not just total cycle time. Aggregate numbers hide where the waste actually lives.
Loading-phase waste (under-filled buckets, oversized rock from poor fragmentation, loader misalignment) shows up downstream as low payload and slow cycles — trace it back to the face, not the truck.
Dumping-phase delays are often a dozer/tip-face problem, not a truck problem — poor floor level or queuing at the dump adds dead time that looks like a hauling issue.

Operator variability is the single biggest lever ADW's own Kaizen work identified — two operators on the same route, same truck, can post meaningfully different cycle times. That's a coaching gap, not an equipment gap.

ADW doesn't currently capture per-stage cycle time in any workbook — only aggregate distance/time and delay-reason codes. A one-shift manual time-motion study by a foreman is the only way to see the real breakdown right now.
apply: Next time you're at a loading face or dump point, time one full cycle by stage on your phone — if idle or queue time is eating more than load or haul time, that's your bottleneck, not the truck count.
